description.value: The study examined fronto-limbic activation and functional connectivity in unaffected youth at familial risk for bipolar disorder during an emotional working memory paradigm.

spans.text: The current study aimed to address this question by examining the functioning of fronto-limbic systems in unaffected youth at familial risk for BD using an fMRI emotional working memory paradigm

value: we hypothesized that relative to healthy control participants, these unaffected offspring at familial risk of BD would exhibit reduced VLPFC activation and increased amygdala activation during the attentional demand condition with emotional distracters.
we hypothesized that relative to healthy control youth, offspring at risk of BD would exhibit reduced VLPFC modulation of the amygdala to emotional distracters in the attentional demand condition.
